title: Haryana audit finds suspected embezzlement and incomplete works in state departments
dek: The CAG's composite audit for the year ended March 2024 records suspected embezzlement of ₹40.51 lakh and payment of ₹6.37 crore for incomplete work, among other findings.
indiaConnection: This audit examines how a public programme in Haryana was carried out and recorded, and it states what the audited record can and cannot establish for the people in India who depend on it.

eventTime.label: Date not established in the supplied evidence

body.text: The audit record for the year ended March 2024 reports suspected embezzlement of ₹40.51 lakh in the Information, Public Relations and Languages Department. It also reports that the Directorate of Secondary Education used the same vouchers twice, leading to suspected embezzlement of ₹3.95 lakh. These figures appear in the audit's compliance observations, but the record does not state who is alleged to have committed the embezzlement or how the amounts were detected.

The audit does not provide a narrative of events leading to these suspected embezzlements. It only records the amounts and the departments involved. A reader cannot infer from this record whether any disciplinary action was taken or whether the amounts were recovered.

At Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University in Hisar, the audit notes a ₹6.37 crore payment for work that was not completed. It also mentions that a bank guarantee's terms were relaxed, causing the bio-gas plant's goal to be missed. These two items are listed together in the audit, yet no causal link is drawn between them.

section.title: Payments for incomplete work and other lapses

body.text: The Higher Education Department is said to have spent money wastefully on equipment and services because procurement happened without checking what users actually needed. The audit also says that payments went out without confirming the expected results of start-up incubators and the e-karma project. These are distinct observations with their own backgrounds, but the total wasteful spending is not quantified.

The audit is a composite report for the year ended March 2024, covering civil departments of the Government of Haryana. It includes a chapter on sewage and sewerage management in urban areas, but the supplied evidence does not include details of that chapter. The record's scope is limited to the period and sample it names, and it does not claim to cover all departments or all transactions.

section.title: What the audit covers and what it does not

body.text: The audit also notes non-verification of bills and vouchers at worksites, non-constitution of a vigilance cell and quality monitors, and issues with social audits and mandatory records. These observations are listed in the table of contents, but the supplied evidence does not include the detailed findings. Therefore, the record supports the existence of these observations but not their full content.

perspectives.label: Auditor
perspectives.rationale: The audit is an independent examination of the institution's records, and its perspective is to identify deviations from rules and procedures.
perspectives.sees: The audit sees specific instances of suspected embezzlement, incomplete work, and procedural lapses.
perspectives.values: It values adherence to financial rules and proper documentation.
perspectives.uses: It uses the institution's own records to identify discrepancies.
perspectives.mayMiss: It may miss the operational reasons behind the lapses or the impact on beneficiaries.

contextBridge.question: How do audit findings shape public trust in government spending?
contextBridge.connection: This audit record provides a basis for citizens to question whether public funds are being used as intended, but it does not by itself establish the full picture of accountability.
